g.text: The written submission carries the whole argument.
The live session adds proof, not new story.
Two tracks. One is what they read with nobody in the room to explain it. The other is what happens on the day, where the demonstration lead runs the chosen scenarios in the live technology.
TRACK A · WRITTEN SUBMISSION · SLIDES 01 TO 13 OF THIS SECTION
WHAT THE TECHNOLOGY SECTION HAS TO ANSWER, AND WHERE IT IS ANSWERED
All the tools from brief through to delivery
Tracking what has already been executed, so second-market demand is ordered, not re-briefed
One slide showing the whole AI task set, because that is what answers their question
about pre, mid and post production.
A separate AI task diagram per scenario. Considered and ruled out. Live session only.
presented live, the same story as the written
all scenarios on one slide, slide 15
their choice, live, in the room
in the actual technology, not a recording
order for the day not agreed
There is no agreed running order for the live day.

The written submission structure is settled: technology, then commercial, then the quality and assurance section. The live day is not. The technology section needs to know what it is handing to, and how long it has, before the
scenario board on slide 15 can be finalised.
Needed from: whoever owns the day.
TECHNOLOGY SECTION · STORYBOARD FOR NARRATIVE AGREEMENT
